title: docs(plugin-designer): MetadataFieldsPage no longer calls `__proto__` a spec-legal field name (objectui#9787)
body:
Fixes #9787

Clause-②: no

## What this changes

Comment-only, in three rounds, plus an empty-frontmatter changeset. Round 1 is `packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataFieldsPage.tsx` (inside `toFieldsMap`); rounds 2 and 3 fold in the unheld siblings of the same claim, on the seat's order.

- The `Why Object.fromEntries` docblock no longer says `__proto__` is a SPEC-LEGAL field name, and no longer quotes the 17.2.0 `success = true` reading. It now dates the contract change: through `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 the body was accepted; since 17.5.0 it is refused at `fields.__proto__` by a pre-parse guard, and `constructor` / `prototype` are refused on the same map by a reserved-name rule. It keeps the half that is still true: building the map by assignment would invoke the prototype setter and drop the field, so the spec's refusal could never name it. The `__proto__` verdict points at the instrument that re-measures it (`describe('the instrument')` in `MetadataFieldsPage.fieldsMapKeying.test.tsx`). The comment also says that nothing in this package re-measures the `constructor` / `prototype` half.
- The own-property read of `prevFields[name]` no longer calls `__proto__` and `constructor` "the two spec-legal names". It now says why the guard still matters on 17.5.0: the read runs before the PUT that the spec judges, `FieldDesigner` takes a free-text name, and a document stored before 17.5.0 can still carry either name.
- Round 2, the unheld siblings of the same claim: `packages/app-shell/src/services/MetadataService.ts`, the `toFieldsMap` and `previousFieldEntry` docblocks, which said `__proto__` is a SPEC-LEGAL field name. They now date the 17.5.0 change, keep the prototype-setter half, and cite `MetadataService.objectPayloadFieldsMap.test.ts` ("keys a field literally named `__proto__` instead of silently dropping it", "keys the record with a snake_case rule") and `MetadataService.fieldKeyCarryOver.test.ts` ("does not read `Object.prototype` as a previous entry for a field named `__proto__`").
- Round 2: in `packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataFieldsPage.fieldsMapKeying.test.tsx`, the `PROTO_BODY` docblock now says the fixture models a document stored before 17.5.0 and that the fetch double accepts every PUT. The opaque `inlineHelpText` marker changed from "Stored under a legal name." to "Stored before the spec refused this name." at both of its sites, so the round-trip assertion still compares the served value with the saved one.
- Round 3: the pending `.changeset/writefields-proto-key-9237.md` (an app-shell patch, which publishes verbatim into the CHANGELOG) carried the same claim: "`__proto__` is a spec-legal stored field key, so the mutilated document was ACCEPTED". It gets the house dated, append-only note ("Correction, 2026-10-01 (objectui#9787)"), with the frontmatter and existing paragraphs byte-identical. The note says the claim held through 17.4.0, that since 17.5.0 an own `__proto__` key is refused at `fields.__proto__`, and that a body which has already lost the key is still accepted, so the `Object.fromEntries` fix stays load-bearing.

## Premise check, measured on the branch base `1563d3e10`

- **H1 holds.** The installed `@objectstack/spec` is 17.5.0, both in `pnpm-lock.yaml` and in the resolved package. I probed the installed `ObjectSchema` with a `fields` map in which `__proto__` is an own key:
  - a plain field gives `success=true` (the positive control is lit);
  - `__proto__` gives `custom @ fields.__proto__`;
  - `constructor` and `prototype` give `custom @ fields`, with the message `Field names must not be "constructor" or "prototype"`;
  - `Bad Name` gives `invalid_key @ fields.Bad Name` (the refusal path is lit).

  For a dark control I ran the same probe on the 17.4.0 tarball. There, `__proto__` parses green and is dropped from the output, and `constructor` / `prototype` parse green.

  One correction to the card body: the key grammar does not refuse `constructor` / `prototype`, since both match `/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/`. A separate reserved-name refine on the map refuses them, and the comment says so.
- **H2 holds, so neither pin was edited.** Both pins already state the 17.5.0 behaviour:
  - `MetadataService.objectPayloadFieldsMap.test.ts` pins `custom @ fields.__proto__`, in the test "keys the record with a snake_case rule — `__proto__` matches it, and the spec refuses it BY NAME".
  - `object-fields-io.prototypeKey-9237.test.ts` pins that 17.5.0 refuses the kept key by name, in the test "the spec still ACCEPTS the mutilated body".
- **H3 holds.** Both sentences were present, as the card says, and this PR rewrites them.

## H4: what the objectui doors do with a field named `__proto__`

These were one-off probes and are not committed.

**plugin-designer (`MetadataFieldsPage` plus `FieldDesigner`).** The probe used the real page, the real `FieldDesigner`, the real `DrawerForm` and the real `MetadataClient`. Only the grid was mocked, as the package's own tests do. The name was typed into the real add-field drawer.

The transport is a gate double. It parses the PUT with `JSON.parse` (the semantics of Hono's `c.req.json()`, which keep an own `__proto__` key) and runs the installed 17.5.0 `ObjectSchema`. On failure it answers 422 `INVALID_METADATA` in the dispatcher shape, with the `/meta` headline message. The double is modelled on objectstack `metadata-protocol` `specValidationFindings`, read at objectstack `95fed33a`; it is not a live server.

| typed name | PUTs | own key on the wire | gate verdict | page error surface |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `probe_ok` (control) | 1 | yes | pass | none |
| `__proto__` | 1 | yes | `custom @ fields.__proto__` | `object/probe_widget failed spec validation: 1 issue — fields.__proto__ [custom]` |
| `constructor` | 1 | yes | `custom @ fields` | `… 1 issue — fields [custom]` |
| `prototype` | 1 | yes | `custom @ fields` | `… 1 issue — fields [custom]` |
| `Bad Name` (control) | 1 | yes | `invalid_key @ fields.Bad Name` | `… 1 issue — fields.Bad Name [invalid_key]` |

The designer checks no name against the grammar, so it treats `__proto__` exactly like `Bad Name`. The name reaches the wire intact and the spec's refusal reaches the author. Nothing is stored, and nothing is dropped silently.

**Studio (app-shell metadata-admin).** Studio's name normalizer cannot produce `__proto__`: `toFieldNameLoose('__proto__')` gives `proto_` and `toFieldName` gives `proto`. `constructor` and `prototype` pass the normalizer unchanged, and the live client validator (`validateMetadataDraft('object', …)` over the installed spec) refuses them with the reserved-name message. A stored `__proto__` field is kept by the `object-fields-io` writer and refused live at `fields.__proto__`, with the spec's message.

So no published objectui door accepts a name the spec refuses, and under the claim this card is prose only.

## Changeset: empty frontmatter instead of the suggested patch

The dispatch suggested a `@object-ui/plugin-designer` patch. Following the precedent of objectui#10150 and objectui#10159, I measured the emit instead:

- `toFieldsMap` is not exported.
- The built `dist/` (`.d.ts`, `.js`, `.umd.cjs` and maps) contains none of the new comment text: 0 files match. As a control, a code token from the same file (`metadata-fields-page-error`) is found in `dist/index.js`.
- The comment-stripped TypeScript transpile of the file is byte-identical to the base: the sha256 prefix is `a9d41bf2463f1f10` on both sides, and a one-token code change moves it.

Nothing is released, and the changeset declares that.

app-shell is also declared as releasing nothing, on a measurement:
- neither rewritten function is exported;
- `dist/services/MetadataService.d.ts` carries none of the new text;
- the comment-stripped transpile equals the base (sha256 prefix `9d1616bf2a2d4a8a` on both sides, and a control moves it).

app-shell builds with `tsc`, which keeps comments, so `dist/services/MetadataService.js` does carry the comment text. objectui#10150 and objectui#10159 declared that same state as releasing nothing.

## Gates, round 1 at head `85a959ab4`

- `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-designer^...' --concurrency=2`: 16 of 16 tasks successful, exit 0. This ran at `f4a4867bb`; the later commit adds only the changeset file.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-designer build`, then `type-check` (the script name is echoed): exit 0, exit 0.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-designer/ --maxWorkers=2`: Test Files 31 passed (31), Tests 213 passed (213). 31 is the package's tracked test-file count.
- eslint, narrowed to the changed file, with the three pieces of evidence:
  - the file is in eslint's population (`--print-config` resolves 118 rules, and the package has no config of its own);
  - `--format json` reports 1 file with 0 errors and 0 warnings;
  - type-aware linting is off, so this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.
- Exit 0 from each of these: `check-changeset-presence` (the empty frontmatter is accepted as declared), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check:control-bytes`, `check:installed-pin-claims`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:metadata-write-doors`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:i18n-keys`.
- `check:changeset-claims` flagged the pending `.changeset/6519-retired-field-key-strip.md`, which names this file. I read the paragraph: it is about unifying the retired-key lists, and this change does not make it false.
- `check:doc-examples`: NOT MEASURED. Its prerequisite is not met (18 packages are unbuilt). It reads plugin-designer's `EditorModeToggle` and `useDesignerHistory` examples, not this file, so it is not owed here.

- app-shell closure build: 28 of 28 tasks successful.

- Exit 0 from each of these: `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:control-bytes`, `check-changeset-overwrite`.

## Acceptance notes

These are outside this claim's file surface, so this PR leaves them alone:

- **The same stale claim, one place left.** `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/object-fields-io.ts` has the same claim in the comment on `writeFields`' record branch ("`__proto__` is a spec-legal stored field key"). This file is excluded because objectui#11070 round 5 holds it. Carrier: objectui#11070 (pointer `5922622878`). The other sites this note listed after round 1 are folded in (rounds 2 and 3).
- **Checked and still true.**
  - `MetadataObjectsPage.tsx` notes that object NAMES accept `constructor` and `__proto__`. Measured: 17.5.0 still parses `name: '__proto__'` and `name: 'constructor'`.
  - The prototypeKey pin's "perfectly spec-legal" describes the body that has already lost the key, and 17.5.0 still accepts that body.
- **A reading for the seat.** On the plugin-designer page, a `constructor` or `prototype` refusal reads `fields [custom]` and names no field. Two things combine to cause this:
  - the spec's reserved-name refine reports its issue at `fields`, not at the offending key;
  - the page renders only `err.message`. On the `/meta` door that message is a headline, and the prescription text rides only in `issues[]`, so on this page the author never sees it, for any refusal.
